introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0562 CITIZENSHIP EDUCATION 1, JUNE 2022, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so. Check that this question booklet is headed "ORDINARY LEVEL - 0562 CITIZENSHIP EDUCATION 1". Fill in the information required on the answer sheet using your HB pencil: candidate name, exam session, subject code and candidate identification number. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. If you change your mind about an answer, erase the first mark carefully, then mark your new answer. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces in the question booklet. At the end of the examination, the invigilator shall collect the answer sheet first and then the question booklet. Do not attempt to leave the examination hall with it.
incertitudes: Scan sans couche texte (filigrane gcerevision.com), lu en image page par page (5 pages) ; page de garde vérifiée : ORDINARY LEVEL, 0562 CITIZENSHIP EDUCATION 1, JUNE 2022, QCM de 1h30 (le sujet imprime « one and a half hours »). Aucune figure ni tableau dans le sujet, donc aucune image produite.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les 50 clés sont déduites du programme O Level de Citizenship Education et des institutions du Cameroun. Aucun point imprimé n'a été modifié ; le sujet ne donne pas de barème détaillé (toutes les questions ont le même poids).

Questions où la clé est raisonnée mais discutable (à relire par un enseignant de Citizenship Education) : 8 (professional school pour une future infirmière), 13 (plastiques non biodégradables, mais le bois de chauffe est aussi défendable), 22 (media influence ; depression défendable), 25 (franking machines : mesure de la DGI non vérifiée dans le sujet), 40 (increase unemployment ; smuggling est une forme d'évasion, pas une conséquence), 44 (mediation ; conciliation voisine).

Faits d'institutions à confirmer : Q12 et Q18 (le Ministère de l'Administration territoriale et le Ministère de la Décentralisation et du Développement local se sont partagé leurs compétences dans le temps : tutelle des communes = décentralisation, unités administratives = administration territoriale) ; Q17 et Q19 (rang du Secrétaire général et rôle de l'Inspecteur général auprès du Gouverneur : lecture générale et prudente, aucun texte cité) ; Q28 (loi de 1975 création du Premier ministre, révision de 1979 le rend successeur constitutionnel : date retenue 1979) ; Q29 (1984 : changement de nom en République du Cameroun) ; Q30 (le bilinguisme officiel date de la Constitution fédérale de 1961, donc l'option D est la seule qui n'est pas propre à 1972) ; Q48 (mesure en faveur des minorités ethniques : décentralisation retenue avec réserve).

Converties en questions ouvertes (options ambiguës ou clé non établissable, jamais une lettre au hasard) : 4, 6, 9, 17, 23, 27, 47, 48. 4 : ethnic group (plusieurs options décrivent des unités d'un groupe ethnique, réponse visée D). 6 : le sujet ne dit pas si les feux sont ceux des véhicules ou des piétons (réponse visée A). 9 et 23 : plusieurs causes ou conséquences défendables (A et B). 17 : plusieurs cadres du cabinet du Gouverneur ont un rang élevé (réponse visée B). 27 : devise, drapeau ou hymne défendables (réponse visée A). 47 : plusieurs facteurs de pauvreté des femmes défendables (réponse visée B). 48 : mesure pour les minorités discutable (réponse visée C).
Aucun calcul dans ce sujet : pas de vérification numérique nécessaire.
Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 4, 6, 9, 17, 23, 27, 47, 48.

questions.enonce_markdown: A citizen who displays absolute love and devotion for his/her country is said to be...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Patriotism is love of, and devotion to, one's country, shown by respecting its laws and symbols, serving it and defending its interests. Loyalty is faithfulness to a person, a group or an authority and is a narrower idea; nationalism can be an excessive or exclusive attachment to one's nation; fanaticism is extreme, uncritical enthusiasm.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main purpose of hygiene in the home is to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Hygiene means the practices that keep people and their surroundings clean (washing hands, cleaning the kitchen and toilets, disposing of refuse, keeping water safe). Its main purpose is to stop germs from spreading, that is to prevent illness and disease. Keeping children busy and upholding morals are not the purpose of hygiene, and the saying about cleanliness and godliness only describes an attitude.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: respect cleanliness is next to godliness

questions.enonce_markdown: John's step sister gave birth to a baby boy last year. Who is this boy to John?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A step sister is a sister by the remarriage of a parent, not by blood. Her son is the nephew of John, and because the link passes through a step relationship he is called a step nephew. A sibling is a brother or a sister, a niece is a girl (the baby is a boy), and a cousin is the child of an uncle or an aunt.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
An ethnic group is defined as a group of....

*Options as printed:* A) tribes spread over an extensive region   B) families linked by blood   C) clans covering a large area   D) settlements with common ancestors
questions.corrige_markdown:
An ethnic group is a community of people who share a common ancestry, a common language and a common culture (customs, traditions, beliefs). Several of the printed options describe parts of that idea (families, clans, settlements and tribes are all units of an ethnic group), so the printed question has no single clearly best answer. The option closest to the usual textbook definition is the one that speaks of common ancestors.

**Intended answer: D (settlements with common ancestors).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following is not an institution concerned with family protection?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Non-governmental organisations, religious bodies and traditional authorities all take part in protecting families (counselling, settling disputes, helping vulnerable members, defending children and women). A microfinance institution is a financial body that offers savings and small loans: it is not concerned with family protection.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is Not an appropriate way to avoid road accidents by pedestrians?

*Options as printed:* A) Crossing the road when the green or yellow light is on   B) Crossing the road when the red light is on   C) Crossing where there is zebra crossing   D) Walking on the road facing oncoming traffic
questions.corrige_markdown:
Pedestrians stay safe by crossing at a zebra crossing, by crossing when the traffic has stopped, and by walking on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic so that they can see vehicles coming. When the light facing vehicles is green or yellow, vehicles are moving, so crossing then is dangerous; this is the odd one out. The printed question does not say whether the lights are those of vehicles or of pedestrians, so it can be read the other way round.

**Intended answer: A (Crossing the road when the green or yellow light is on).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The major human cause of road accidents is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A human cause is one that depends on the behaviour of road users, which excludes bad roads and bad weather. Among the human causes, excessive speed is the most common one: it reduces the time a driver has to react, lengthens the braking distance and makes the impact more violent. Dangerous overtaking also causes accidents, but speeding is generally given as the major cause.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: After obtaining GCE Advanced Level, Abanga decides to become a nurse. She should attend a...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Nursing is a profession that is learnt in a specialised training institution (a professional school for health workers) after secondary studies. A technical college trains for technical trades at secondary level, a vocational school trains for manual skills and crafts, and a comprehensive college offers general and technical secondary education together.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select from the list below, the most appropriate reason for which students cheat during examinations.

*Options as printed:* A) Laziness   B) Procrastination   C) Lack of text books   D) Poor teaching by unqualified teachers
questions.corrige_markdown:
Students who do not prepare because they do not want to make the effort of studying are tempted to cheat. Laziness is the personal attitude that is most directly given as the reason for cheating, while procrastination, lack of books and poor teaching are contributing factors that also appear in textbooks. Because several of these options can be defended, the printed question has no single clearly best answer.

**Intended answer: A (Laziness).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: An important economic activity typical of most Cameroonian maritime villages is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Maritime villages are the villages along the Atlantic coast and the estuaries, for example in the Littoral, South West and South Regions. Their people live mainly from the sea and the rivers, so fishing is the activity that is typical of them. Agriculture, trading and hunting are practised in many other places and are not specific to the coast.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An aspect of positive social value in our villages is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A positive social value is a quality that is approved by society and helps people live together. Hospitality, which is welcoming and caring for visitors and strangers, is a positive value in our villages. Superstition, disrespect and dishonesty are negative attitudes.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which Ministry manages councils in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Councils are the basic local authorities of the decentralised system. Their supervision (the supervisory authority over councils) is the responsibility of the Ministry in charge of Decentralisation and Local Development. The Ministry of Territorial Administration looks after the administrative units (regions, divisions, sub-divisions) which are run by appointed officials, not the councils, and the other two ministries have different tasks.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Ministry of Lands, Survey and State Property
Ministry of Decentralisation and Local Development
Ministry of Economy, Planning and Regional Development

questions.enonce_markdown: One way of destroying the environment is by...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Non-biodegradable plastics do not rot: they pile up in soil, gutters, rivers and the sea, block drains and kill animals, so using them carelessly destroys the environment. Replacing the trees that have been cut and using bio-fuels are environmentally friendly practices. Cooking with firewood can contribute to deforestation, but it is a normal household practice and is not the best example of destroying the environment among the options.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One effect of deforestation on the environment is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Deforestation is the clearing of forests. Forests are the homes of animals, birds and insects, so when the trees are felled the habitat is destroyed and many species are threatened. The other options are not the direct effect of deforestation: air pollution comes mainly from smoke and gases, the contamination of water from waste and chemicals, and soil salinisation mostly from irrigation in dry areas.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the reason for the creation of national parks by the government of Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
National parks and other protected areas are set aside by the State to protect and preserve the natural environment: its forests, its wildlife and its landscapes, for the present and future generations. Limiting deforestation and hunting are some of the means used inside a park, and tourism or beauty are secondary benefits, so the general reason is the protection and preservation of nature.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Limit the effect of climate change
Make the environment natural and attractive
Protect and preserve the natural environment

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the Region in Cameroon that shares boundaries with both Nigeria and the Central African Republic.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Adamawa Region lies on the western edge of the country, where it borders Nigeria, and on its eastern side, where it borders the Central African Republic. The Far North and North Regions border Nigeria and Chad, and the East Region borders the Central African Republic, Chad and the Republic of Congo but not Nigeria.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
An administrative official in the Governor's office who has the rank of Senior Divisional Officer is the...

*Options as printed:* A) Private Secretary   B) Secretary General   C) Chief of Cabinet   D) Inspector General
questions.corrige_markdown:
The services of a Regional Governor include a Secretariat General, headed by the Secretary General, who is the senior administrative official of the Governor's services and is generally given the rank of a Senior Divisional Officer. The Private Secretary is a personal assistant of the Governor. The Chief of Cabinet and the Inspector General also hold senior posts in the Governor's services, so the rank attached to each post is not something that can be settled from the question alone.

**Intended answer: B (Secretary General).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: What name is given to the Ministerial department that controls administrative units in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The administrative units (regions, divisions and sub-divisions) are headed by Governors, Senior Divisional Officers and Divisional Officers, who are appointed officials. The ministry that supervises these units is the Ministry of Territorial Administration. The Public Service ministry manages civil servants, the Decentralisation ministry follows the councils and the Supreme State Audit controls public finances.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Ministry of Public Service and Administrative Reforms
Ministry of Decentralisation and Local Development

questions.enonce_markdown: Which Regional official is in charge of the internal control of the services of the Governor, Senior Divisional Officers and Divisional Officers?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the regional administration, the Inspector General is the official who carries out the internal control (inspection) of the services of the Governor and of the Senior Divisional and Divisional Officers of the Region. The Secretary General coordinates administrative work, the Chief of Cabinet handles the Governor's office and the Private Secretary handles his or her personal correspondence.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A practice and inclination to show hatred, bias, mistrust or intolerance towards people with differences in culture and opinion is known as....
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bigotry is stubborn and intolerant attitude towards people who have a different culture, religion or opinion, shown by hatred, bias and mistrust. Nepotism and favouritism mean giving unfair advantages to relatives or to favourites, and tribalism is loyalty to one's own tribe at the expense of others; none of them covers differences of culture and opinion in general.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Criminal or anti-social behaviour of young people best describes ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Juvenile delinquency is the general name for criminal or anti-social behaviour of young people (theft, violence, vandalism, drug dealing, and so on). Prostitution, drug abuse and scamming are particular forms of such behaviour, not the general description.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most important cause of drug abuse in recent times is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Young people today are exposed, through television, films, music and social media, to messages that make drugs look fashionable and harmless, and this influence is generally given as the most important cause of drug abuse in recent times. Health hazards are consequences of drug abuse, not causes, and sexual promiscuity is a related vice. Depression can push someone to drugs, but it is a personal situation rather than a general cause of the present time.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The most outstanding negative consequence of examination malpractices is that...

*Options as printed:* A) it can lead to failure of students   B) it can lead to suspension from the examination   C) it can lead to hatred among the students   D) it can lead to laziness
questions.corrige_markdown:
Examination malpractice is breaking the rules of an examination (copying, impersonation, leaking questions, and so on). The sanction that is most directly attached to it is the suspension or exclusion of the candidate and the cancellation of results, which is why it is given as the most outstanding consequence. Failure, hatred and laziness can follow but are less direct, and the printed options leave room for doubt on which one the question intends.

**Intended answer: B (it can lead to suspension from the examination).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the letter linked to the day set aside by the international community as World AIDS Day.
questions.corrige_markdown:
World AIDS Day is observed every year on 1st December to raise awareness of HIV and AIDS, to show support for people living with HIV and to remember those who have died. 10th December is Human Rights Day, so it should not be confused with it.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: To fight against the use of fake fiscal stamps, the Cameroon government has introduced the...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Fiscal (tax) stamps are paid on many official documents. To stop the circulation of forged stamps, the tax administration has introduced franking machines, which print the proof of payment directly on the document instead of using stamps that can be copied. Printing stamps abroad, inspecting treasury workers and hand scanners are not the measure that is usually quoted.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the meaning of a secular state?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A secular state is a state that is neutral in matters of religion: it has no official religion, it does not favour or punish any religious belief, and it tolerates and protects the right of citizens to practise the religion of their choice. The Constitution of Cameroon declares the State to be secular. The other options describe voting, security and elections, which are not about religion.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Freedom of citizens to vote their leaders

questions.enonce_markdown:
The national symbol that emphasises on the dreams and aspirations of the citizens of that country is...

*Options as printed:* A) the motto   B) the national anthem   C) the seal   D) the flag
questions.corrige_markdown:
The national motto of Cameroon, "Peace - Work - Fatherland", sums up the ideals that the citizens aim at and the values they are asked to live by, so it is the symbol that expresses their dreams and aspirations. The printed question can also be read as pointing to the flag or to the anthem, which carry meanings of hope and unity, so no option is perfectly clear.

**Intended answer: A (the motto).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: In what year was the Cameroon Constitution modified to make the Prime Minister the constitutional successor of the President?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The post of Prime Minister was created in the 1975 amendment of the 1972 Constitution, and it was the constitutional amendment of 1979 that made the Prime Minister the constitutional successor of the President of the Republic in case of vacancy. 1961 is the year of the federal Constitution and 1972 the year of the Constitution that created the unitary State.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the letter linked to the constitutional amendment that changed the name of Cameroon from United Republic of Cameroon to the Republic of Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Constitution of 1972 had created the United Republic of Cameroon. In 1984, a constitutional amendment changed the name of the State to the Republic of Cameroon, which is the name still in use. The 1975 and 1979 amendments dealt with the Prime Minister's office and the 2008 amendment, among other things, with the presidential term.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are provisions of the 1972 constitution except...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The 1972 Constitution put an end to the federation: the provinces replaced the federated states, the United Republic of Cameroon came into being and a single National Assembly replaced the State Assemblies. French and English had already been the official languages since the federal Constitution of 1961, so this was not a new provision of 1972.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the United Republic of Cameroon came to existence
the National Assembly replaced State Assemblies
French and English became the official languages

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify from the list below the function performed by the Judiciary Arm of Government in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The judiciary is the arm of government made up of the courts and tribunals. Its function is to interpret and apply the laws in disputes and to punish offenders. Making laws belongs to the legislature (Parliament), while promulgating laws and signing ordinances are acts of the executive (the President of the Republic).

**Answer: B.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

questions.enonce_markdown: In what ways can the National Assembly of Cameroon control government action?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The National Assembly controls the work of the government by means such as oral and written questions to members of the government, hearings and commissions of enquiry. Defining the policy of the State and appointing or replacing ministers belong to the executive, and persistently blocking government bills would be an abuse and not a normal means of control.

**Answer: D.**
themes: separation of powers and arms of government

choix.texte: By defining the policies of the state
By persistently blocking the passage of government bills

questions.enonce_markdown: At what stage of the electoral process is the announcement of the date that the elections will take place?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Convening the electorate is the official act by which the authority fixes and announces the date of an election and calls the voters to the polls. Voter registration, the production of materials and the campaign are other stages of the electoral process.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: During the convening of the electorate
During the production of election materials

questions.enonce_markdown: The most important way through which a citizen can determine the political future of his/her country is through...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Voting is the right that every adult citizen on the electoral roll can exercise and it is how the people as a whole choose their leaders and decide the direction of the country. Contesting elections and holding public office are open to a few people only, and protest is an occasional means of expressing an opinion.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is not a consequence of an electoral malpractice in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A consequence is a result of the malpractice. Economic stagnation, violence after disputed results and the coming to power of incompetent leaders can all result from rigged elections. Stuffing ballot boxes (putting in fake ballot papers) is itself a form of electoral malpractice, not a consequence of it.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What role does distribution play in the economic process of production?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Production is complete only when goods and services reach the people who will use them. Distribution is the stage that brings goods from the producer, through wholesalers and retailers, to the final consumer, so that they are available where and when they are needed. Transport is only one of the services that help distribution.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It transports goods from place to place
It makes goods and services available to the final consumer
It links the consumer to the buyer
It encourages the provision of transport means

questions.enonce_markdown: Select a letter that matches with a social security scheme aimed at protecting the wellbeing of children in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Family allowances are the benefits paid under the social security system to workers who have children, to help them bring up and educate their children. A pension is paid to retired workers, a housing allowance concerns accommodation and there is no social security scheme called a labour allowance.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Economic growth may not necessarily mean economic development because of...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Economic growth is an increase in the output of a country, while economic development also means a better life for the people (health, education, jobs, less poverty). When capital flight takes the money out of the country, the growth does not benefit its people and does not lead to development. Investment and low military spending help development.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is a custom duty?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A customs duty is a tax charged on goods that enter (or, sometimes, leave) the country, collected at the border by the customs service. It brings revenue to the State and can also protect local industries. A tax on each stage of production is a value added tax, and a tax on income is an income tax.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Tax levied on each stage of production
Tax levied on home produced goods
Tax levied on imported goods to raise money
Tax levied on an individual's income

questions.enonce_markdown: Tax evasion could cause the economy to experience...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tax evasion is the illegal refusal to pay taxes. The State then loses revenue, can no longer finance public services and investments that create jobs, and unemployment tends to increase. Smuggling is a way of evading taxes rather than a result of it, and dumping is the sale of goods abroad at very low prices. The printed options leave some doubt on which result the question has in mind.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Inalienable rights refer to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Inalienable rights are rights that belong to every human being from birth and that cannot be taken away, sold or given up, for example the right to life. Civic and political rights, the rights of citizens and the right of association are categories of rights but are not defined by the fact that they cannot be taken away.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: rights of belonging to an association

questions.enonce_markdown: Torture is a Human Rights violation mainly because it...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Torture is the deliberate infliction of severe physical or mental suffering. It is a violation of human rights above all because it attacks the dignity of the person, that is, it treats a human being as an object and degrades him or her. Causing pain is part of what torture is, but the reason why it is condemned so firmly is the loss of human dignity.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is not an instrument put in place by the Cameroon government to protect the rights of citizens?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Penal Code punishes offences against persons and property, the Labour Code protects workers and the Civil Servants Status Code protects the rights of public servants. The Highway Code lays down the rules of road traffic, so it regulates the behaviour of road users and is not an instrument for protecting citizens' rights.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A third party helps two parties in a dispute to agree. That conflict has been resolved through...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In mediation, a neutral third party helps the two sides to talk and to find an agreement themselves, without imposing a solution. In negotiation the parties talk directly, with no third party, and in arbitration the third party listens and then imposes a binding decision. Conciliation is close to mediation, but mediation is the usual word for a third party helping parties to agree.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a feature not associated with good governance.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Good governance means that power is used in a way that is accountable, transparent and lawful: it includes respect for human rights, the rule of law and independent electoral bodies. A powerful executive that is not checked by the other arms of government is a sign of weak governance, so it is not a feature of good governance.

**Answer: B.**
themes: good governance and the rule of law

choix.texte: Respect for the rule of law

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is the most common cause of conflicts between states?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Conflicts between states are mostly caused by disputes over borders (frontier violations), for example over the control of a territory or of its resources. Regional inequality and the violation of a constitution are internal matters of a single state, and cultural differences are rarely a direct cause of war between states.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select an important factor that has rendered most women poor in Africa.

*Options as printed:* A) They lack access to education   B) They are restricted to domestic and child bearing activities   C) They are forced into early marriages   D) They have no right to inherit
questions.corrige_markdown:
In many African societies women are mainly expected to do domestic work and to bear and raise children, which keeps them away from paid jobs, land ownership and decisions, and so leaves them poor. Lack of education, early marriage and denial of inheritance rights are also real causes of poverty among women, so the printed options leave room for doubt on which one the question intends.

**Intended answer: B (They are restricted to domestic and child bearing activities).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
One measure taken by the government to specifically promote the interest of ethnic minorities is...

*Options as printed:* A) award of scholarships   B) promotion of bilingualism   C) administrative decentralisation   D) granting of special status
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Constitution of Cameroon states that the State protects minorities and preserves the rights of indigenous populations. In the decentralised system, representatives of these populations are meant to be included in the regional bodies, and this is the measure that is most closely tied to minorities among the options. Scholarships and bilingualism are not aimed at ethnic minorities, and a special status is a different kind of measure; the printed options leave room for doubt on which one the question intends.

**Intended answer: C (administrative decentralisation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: In what major way has globalisation socially affected the world in recent times?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Globalisation is the growing interconnection of countries through trade, travel, communication and migration. Its social effects include the quick spread of diseases from one country to another (as seen with epidemics) as people move around the world. An increase in output and capital flight are economic effects, and the United Nations was created in 1945, long before the recent wave of globalisation.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Terrorists use the following methods to achieve their objectives EXCEPT...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Terrorists use violence and fear (harassment, hijackings, kidnappings, bomb attacks, hostage taking) to force governments or populations to give in to their demands. Lobbying is a peaceful and legal way of influencing decision makers and is not used by terrorists as a method of terror.

**Answer: D.**
